Position Information Position Information Working Title Extension Instructor or Open Rank Extension Educator - Early Childhood (Dawson County) Department NE Ext Engagement Zone 3-12352 Requisition Number F_260021 Posting Open Date 02/23/2026 Application Review Date: (To ensure consideration, please submit all application materials before review date) 08/17/2026 Posting Close Date Open Until Filled Yes Description of Work OVERVIEWThis position is based in Lexington, NE with the geographic accountability region of Arthur, McPherson, Logan, Custer, Dawson, Lincoln, Perkins and Keith Counties. Focused on young children and their caregivers (e.g., parents, early childhood teachers), this position will contribute to the integrated (extension, research, and teaching) land-grant mission of the home unit and the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources as an effective scholar and citizen. The primary responsibility for this position is to develop and deliver high quality, innovative educational programs and resources as an active participant in the work of the Early Childhood team and may be active in a statewide issue team that addresses current issues facing Nebraska. This position is expected to interact closely with parents, teachers, early childhood professionals, and caregivers of young children in their geographic area and possibly statewide based on the current projects and goals of the Early Childhood team. Nebraska Extension’s Early Childhood team supports adults who play a role in young children’s lives by providing educational programming and resources about early child development and early care and education. Adults play a significant role in setting the stage for young children’s lifelong learning, discovery, and success. The Early Childhood team is committed to empowering these adults to support and provide effective learning experiences for Nebraska’s young children. Such early learning experiences enhance children’s readiness (physical, cognitive, social, and emotional) for school and setting them up for lifelong success.This twelve-month, non-tenure track position carries the title of open rank extension educator or extension instructor, depending on the candidate’s level of education. Those possessing a graduate-level degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an educator position, a full-time, promotable, non-tenure track appointment. Those in possession of an undergraduate degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an instructor position, a full-time, non-promotable, non-tenure track appointment that will be renewed annually for a maximum of five years in the appointment. If hired as an instructor, the incumbent will be expected to make satisfactory progress toward and complete a master’s degree within the initial five-year appointment period. As part of the Nebraska benefits package, UNL offers tuition remission for full-time employees, up to 15 credit hours per year. Once the master’s degree is earned within that period, the position will advance to an assistant extension educator appointment. Develops and delivers proactive, innovative, and engaging educational programs and products, using teaching methods and strategies that have significant reach, engagement, and impact in your county, accountability region, and, as appropriate, statewide and nationally. Establishes and sustains a strong local and regional clientele base and programming portfolio that is documented and shared with colleagues. Employs innovative strategies and technologies to design, develop, implement, and assess programs for a strong Extension education program/engagement at the county, accountability region, and statewide levels. Engages and teaches in a collaborative learning and problem-solving environment, working with assistants, educators, and specialists to encourage learners to adopt research-based decision-making information. jobs.title: HVAC Instructor
jobs.description: Privacy PolicyJob OpeningsHVAC InstructorHVAC - Norfolk, NebraskaNortheast Community College is seeking an individual to fill an HVAC Instructor position at the Norfolk campus. This position is eligible for Northeast Community College’s excellent full-time faculty fringe benefit package, including: College-paid health insurance premiums for single, employee/spouse, employee/children or family plans College-paid employee dental premiums College paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance Competitive rates for vision plans and dependent dental Up to 9.5% matching on 403(b) retirement plan BestCare EAP Flex spending plans This position is an in-person, on campus faculty position. Under minimal supervision, the HVAC Instructor is responsible for delivering high-quality instruction in HVACR technology across a variety of instructional formats and locations. The instructor will support student learning and success while developing and maintaining curriculum aligned with industry standards and workforce needs. Instructional emphasis includes residential, commercial, and industrial heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) systems; system installation, design, and maintenance; electrical components and controls; airflow distribution and psychometrics; refrigerant handling and piping systems; and troubleshooting and repair techniques. The instructor will also integrate safety standards, energy efficiently principles, sustainability practices, and emerging technologies relevant to the HVACR industry. The instructor must be able to read and interpret technical documents such as safety regulations, HVACR codes, blueprints, and installation manuals. Responsibilities include documenting student progress, maintaining accurate records, and utilizing instructional technologies and tools relevant to the trade. Additionally, the instructor will collaborate with faculty and staff to ensure a high-quality educational experience for a diverse student population while adhering to the College’s mission, policies, and procedures. Hours of instruction for this position will be primarily afternoons and evenings, Monday through Thursday, and all day Friday. Morning work hours will be required occasionally. Requirements: Education: Requires an associate’s degree in HVACR Technology, Construction Technology, or a closely related field. Bachelor’s degree preferred. A combination of licensure and/or certification in conjunction with work experience may be considered in the absence of a college degree. Must hold (or be willing to obtain) EPA 608 Certified, Forklift Certification, National Coalition of Certification Centers Train-The-Trainer Certification, and other industry certifications preferred. Experience: Minimum of three years of hands-on experience in HVACR installation, maintenance and repair. Experience in residential, commercial and industrial systems preferred. Skills: Strong knowledge of HVACR systems, materials, and installation techniques. Proficiency in reading and applying HAVACR codes, blueprints, and schematics. Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVACR systems. Knowledge of safety practices, tools, and equipment used in the HVACR trade. Ability to effectively communicate technical information verbally and in writing. Basic computer skills and ability to use instructional technologies. Commitment to student success and inclusive teaching practices. Special Instructions to Applicant: Applicants selected for an interview will be expected to provide a 10–15-minute teaching presentation that covers refrigeration cycle and its application in residential HVAC systems to the search committee (students). Position is open until filled.
